results.notes: A location phrase meaning on the body or with someone personally.

examples.translation: I don't have any money on me right now.
My younger brother is all wet.

results.notes: This can mean the body itself or a person's health.

examples.translation: I'm not feeling very well physically.
Grandpa is in very good health.

results.notes: The basic question word for asking what.

examples.translation: What fruit do you want to eat?
What is the teacher saying?

results.notes: A common verb for becoming sick.

examples.translation: My younger brother got sick and needs to see a doctor.
Mom got sick and is resting at home.

results.notes: Use this when someone gets angry or is angry.

examples.translation: Dad got angry and isn't talking.
Don't be angry. I know I was wrong.

results.notes: The common noun for a birthday.

examples.translation: Today is my birthday.
I was very happy on my birthday.

results.notes: The number ten.

examples.translation: My home has ten cups.
My older sister is ten years old this year.

results.notes: A common noun for a time or moment.

examples.translation: I lived in Beijing when I was little.
Mom doesn't talk when she's busy.

results.notes: A common noun for time.

examples.translation: I don't have time to read right now.
It's time for class, so let's go quickly.

results.notes: A common noun for a thing, task, or matter.

examples.translation: I have a lot to do today.
I know about this matter.

results.notes: The basic verb for trying something.

examples.translation: Try this bag first for a moment.
Try this dish for a moment.

results.notes: The basic verb meaning to be.

examples.translation: He is my friend.
This place is the school.

results.notes: A common yes-no question pattern.

examples.translation: Are you our teacher?
Is this your bag?

results.notes: The common noun for a hand.

examples.translation: My younger brother's hands are very clean.
There is water on my hand.

results.notes: The everyday word for a mobile phone.

examples.translation: My mobile phone is on the table.
Mom is using her cell phone to make a call.

results.notes: The common noun for a book.

examples.translation: I bought three books today.
This book is very good.

results.notes: The everyday word for a schoolbag.

examples.translation: My schoolbag is on the bed.
Mom bought a new schoolbag.

results.notes: A common noun for a bookstore.

examples.translation: There is a bookstore next to the school.
I'm going to the bookstore this afternoon to buy books.

results.notes: The common noun for a tree.

examples.translation: There are many trees at the school.
The trees over there look very nice.

results.notes: The common noun for water.

examples.translation: I want to drink water now.
There is water in this cup.

results.notes: A common noun for fruit in general.

examples.translation: Mom is going to the shop to buy fruit.
All this fruit is very tasty.

results.notes: The basic verb for sleeping.

examples.translation: My younger brother is sleeping on the bed.
I'm too tired and want to sleep.

results.notes: A very common everyday phrase for sleeping.

examples.translation: The child goes to sleep at nine in the evening.
I go to sleep as soon as I get home at night.

results.notes: A common verb for saying something or speaking a language.

examples.translation: The teacher said there isn't class today.
Mom can also speak Chinese.

results.notes: A common verb for talking or speaking.

examples.translation: Don't talk in class.
My younger brother can talk now.
